newsitem.title: UK: Zambian HIV-positive doctor sacked in Britain.
newsitem.headline: Zambian HIV-positive doctor sacked in Britain.

text.p: An HIV-positive junior doctor who continued working for almost nine months after being told his lover had contracted the virus was sacked on Tuesday for endangering the lives of his patients.

The General Medical Council (GMC), which governs Britain's doctors, said Zambian-born Patrick Ngosa had resorted to a "series of blatant lies" when asked about the relationship with the woman, named only as Mrs A.

Ngosa, who specialised in obstetrics and gynaecology, repeatedly denied the two had ever had sex. In fact, he continued working after she told him she had the HIV virus and he only agreed to a test some eight and a half months later.

The GMC announced it was striking Ngosa off the medical register of approved doctors with immediate effect, saying he had betrayed his patients' trust and undermined public confidence in the medical profession.
Around 7,000 worried former patients in southern England contacted health services after Ngosa's condition was revealed.
Ngosa was not present at the hearing. Unconfirmed reports say he has returned to Zambia with his family.
